question.text: Prakriti Cat III AIF holds 1,00,000 shares of a thinly-traded SME. Daily traded volume = 25,000 shares. Current market price = INR 100. Daily price band = -2% (lower). Opportunity cost = 12% p.a. (ignore intra-day discounting for simplicity). Over how many trading days must the fund liquidate, and at approximately what un-discounted sale price on Day T+3?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the illiquid-security valuation illustration in the workbook (pages 399-401), days to liquidate = position / daily volume = 1,00,000 / 25,000 = 4 days. Each day's price applies the -2% lower band so price multiplies by 0.98. Series: T = 100; T+1 = 98; T+2 = 96.04; T+3 = 100 x 0.98^3 = approximately 94.12. The Trap: 2 days uses incorrect volume math. 5 days overshoots the position-divided-by-ADV figure. 3 days stops at T+2 and misses the T+3 step. Note: The 4-day liquidation, the lower-price-band sequence, and the opportunity-cost discounting framework all appear in pages 399-401; the un-discounted Day T+3 price is the 0.98^3 product of the starting price.
